provenance: Batch b31: the proofs al-Mughnī and its peers cite for each position, weighed by an agent under docs/architecture/taarud-reconciliation.md §redesign (tiers per Rawḍa v02 p389–390, murajjiḥāt per Rawḍa and al-Kawkab); every excerpt located verbatim; qaṭʿī and ijmāʿ tiers reviewed. No human review yet.

proofs.dalil: Q 4:43 «nor when junub, except passing through, until you have washed»: ghusl is made the limit of the bar from prayer, so once he has washed he is not barred
proofs.excerpt_ar: جعل الغسل غاية للمنع من الصلاة، فإذا اغتسل يجب أن لا يمنع منها
proofs.note: The āya is about the junub. It bears on someone with both ḥadaths only through the implied sense of the ghāya: zanni.

proofs.dalil: They are two acts of worship of one kind, so the lesser enters the greater, as ʿumra enters ḥajj
proofs.excerpt_ar: ولأنهما عبادتان من جنس واحد، فتدخل الصغرى في الكبرى، كالعمرة في الحج
proofs.note: Analogy with ʿumra in ḥajj: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr: God required ghusl of the junub, not wuḍūʾ («and if you are junub, purify yourselves», Q 5:6); one who washes his whole body has done what is due, «an ijmāʿ with no disagreement»
proofs.excerpt_ar: لأن الله تعالى إنما افترض على الجنب الغسل من الجنابة، دون الوضوء، بقوله {وإن كنتم جنبا فاطهروا}
proofs.who: Ibn Qudāma, al-Mughnī (quoting Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr)
proofs.note: The āya by its apparent sense, with an ijmāʿ reported by one transmitter and contradicted by the riwāya and al-Shāfiʿī's other view that al-Mughnī reports on the same page: zanni.

proofs.dalil: The Prophet did wuḍūʾ (with his ghusl)
proofs.excerpt_ar: وهو أحد قولي الشافعي؛ لأن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فعل ذلك
proofs.note: The riwāya (and one of al-Shāfiʿī's views) that ghusl does not suffice for wuḍūʾ. A marfūʿ report of his deed: zanni.

proofs.dalil: Both the janāba and the ḥadath occurred, so both purifications are due, as when each occurs alone
proofs.excerpt_ar: ولأن الجنابة والحدث وجدا منه، فوجبت لهما الطهارتان، كما لو كانا مفردين
proofs.note: Analogy with each ḥadath occurring alone: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Where the day of arrival falls in Ramaḍān he must make it up, because he did not fast it for his vow (Kashshāf applies the same to a month from the day of arrival that begins on the first of Ramaḍān)
proofs.excerpt_ar: وإن وافق قدومه يوما من رمضان فعليه القضاء) لأنه لم يصمه عن نذره
proofs.note: The fast was not done for the vow, so the vow still has to be made up. A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: al-Qāḍī: the vow is valid, being a vow of obedience that can usually be fulfilled, as if the month had fallen in Shaʿbān; so he fasts Ramaḍān, then makes up the vow and expiates
proofs.excerpt_ar: والصحيح عندي صحة النذر؛ لأنه نذر طاعة يمكن الوفاء به غالبا، فانعقد، كما لو وافق شعبان. فعلى هذا يصوم رمضان، ثم يقضي، ويكفر
proofs.note: al-Qāḍī's preferred view, also Abū Bakr's choice: Ramaḍān does not settle the vow. qiyas.

proofs.dalil: He vowed a fast in a stretch of time and has fasted in it; this is the analogue (qiyās) of the view of Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿIkrima
proofs.excerpt_ar: وهو قياس قول ابن عباس، وعكرمة؛ لأنه نذر صوما في وقت، وقد صام فيه
proofs.note: al-Khiraqī's ruling: one fast counts for both Ramaḍān and the vow. A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Ibn ʿAbbās, on one who vowed ḥajj before performing the obligatory ḥajj: one ḥajj counts for both (he approved ʿIkrima's analogy with a vowed four rakʿas prayed as ʿaṣr); Ibn ʿUmar and Anas held that he starts with the ḥajj of Islam and then performs the vow
proofs.excerpt_ar: وروى عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، في رجل نذر أن يحج، ولم يكن حج الفريضة، قال: يجزئ لهما جميعا
proofs.note: al-Mughnī cites this in support of al-Khiraqī's view. It concerns the parallel ḥajj case, and Ibn ʿUmar and Anas disagree in the same passage, so the tier is aqrabSahabi. It would be qiyas if the carry-over from ḥajj to fasting counts as the proof.

proofs.dalil: The zakāt is itself a ṣadaqa, so one payment counts for zakāt and the vow, and the rest is ṣadaqa for the vow
proofs.excerpt_ar: إلا أن ينوي الزكاة بقدرها، ويكون ذلك صدقة تجزئه عن الزكاة والنذر؛ لكون الزكاة صدقة
proofs.note: al-Mughnī's iḥtimāl (position 0). A stated ʿilla: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Each of them is a ṣadaqa, as when one intends both the greeting of the mosque and the regular sunna with two rakʿas
proofs.excerpt_ar: الزكاة والنذر إن نواهما معا) لأن كلا منهما صدقة كما لو نوى بركعتين التحية والراتبة
proofs.note: Analogy with two rakʿas intended for the taḥiyya and the rātiba: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: The Prophet's command that the pilgrim's last act be at the House («until his last act is at the House»): this ṭawāf is his last act, so the command is fulfilled
proofs.excerpt_ar: إحداهما، يجزئه عن طواف الوداع، لأنه أمر أن يكون آخر عهده بالبيت، وقد فعل
proofs.note: The first riwāya (al-Khiraqī). A marfūʿ ḥadīth whose wording is met by the ziyāra ṭawāf, through its apparent sense: zanni.

proofs.dalil: What is prescribed as a greeting of the mosque is satisfied by an obligatory act of its kind, as the prescribed prayer satisfies the two rakʿas of taḥiyyat al-masjid
proofs.excerpt_ar: ولأن ما شرع لتحية المسجد أجزأ عنه الواجب من جنسه، كتحية المسجد بركعتين تجزئ عنهما المكتوبة
proofs.note: Analogy with taḥiyyat al-masjid: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: They are two obligatory acts of worship, so neither counts for the other, like two obligatory prayers
proofs.excerpt_ar: وعنه، لا يجزئه عن طواف الوداع؛ لأنهما عبادتان واجبتان، فلم تجز إحداهما عن الأخرى، كالصلاتين الواجبتين
proofs.note: The case records this side as a takhrīj; al-Mughnī reports it as a riwāya and gives this reason. Analogy with two obligatory prayers: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Same: they differ, like two obligatory prayers, and as when one intends the farewell ṭawāf for the ziyāra
proofs.excerpt_ar: والثانية: لا، لاختلافهما كالصلاتين الواجبتين، وكما لو نوى بطوافه الوداع عن طواف الزيارة
proofs.note: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: The ḥadīth of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Zayd b. al-Khaṭṭāb: «and if two witnesses testify, then fast and break the fast»: the fiṭr is tied to two witnesses
proofs.excerpt_ar: أحدهما: لا يفطرون؛ لقوله - عليه السلام -: «وإن شهد اثنان فصوموا وأفطروا»
proofs.note: First wajh: they do not break the fast after thirty days begun on one witness. A marfūʿ āḥād report whose bearing here is by its implied sense (two witnesses for the fiṭr): zanni.

proofs.dalil: Breaking the fast may not rest on one witness, as when one man testifies to the Shawwāl crescent (aṣl: Shawwāl crescent; ʿilla: a fiṭr resting on a single witness)
proofs.excerpt_ar: ولأنه فطر، فلم يجز أن يستند إلى شهادة واحد، كما لو شهد بهلال شوال
proofs.note: Analogy with the testimony to the Shawwāl crescent, which needs two: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Stated rationale: lest the fiṭr come about on the word of one man
proofs.excerpt_ar: أشهرهما لا يفطرون لئلا يؤدي إلى الفطر بقول واحد
proofs.note: Ibn Rajab's reason for the better-known wajh: a stated rationale, qiyas.

proofs.dalil: The fiṭr follows from completing the count, not from the testimony, and what is not established on its own can be established as a dependent, as lineage follows a birth proven by women's testimony
proofs.excerpt_ar: لأن الصوم إذا وجب الفطر لاستكمال العدة، لا بالشهادة، وقد يثبت تبعا ما لا يثبت أصلا
proofs.note: Second wajh (al-Mughnī notes it is al-Shāfiʿī's naṣṣ and reported from Abū Ḥanīfa): the fiṭr follows the fast. Analogy with lineage proven through a birth to which women testify: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Same: the fiṭr is established as a dependent of the fast, as lineage is established through a birth proven by women
proofs.excerpt_ar: والثاني وجزم به في " الوجيز " أنهم يفطرون لثبوته تبعا، كالنسب لا يثبت بشهادة النساء، ويثبت بها الولادة
proofs.note: al-Mubdiʿ repeats the tabaʿ analogy for the second wajh (al-Wajīz affirms it): qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Praying tarāwīḥ that night is a precaution for the sunna of its night prayer and entails nothing forbidden, unlike advancing the fast; Aḥmad's word «al-qiyām qabl al-ṣiyām»
proofs.excerpt_ar: القيام قبل الصيام احتياط لسنة قيامه، ولا يتضمن محذورا، والصوم نهي عن تقديمه
proofs.note: al-Majd's argument for praying tarāwīḥ on the cloudy night, as the night prayer follows the precautionary fast. A stated rationale (iḥtiyāṭ) built on Aḥmad's word: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: He prays tarāwīḥ that night as a precaution for the sunna; the fast's other dependents follow because they depend on the fast
proofs.excerpt_ar: (ويصلي التراويح ليلته) إذن (احتياطا للسنة) قال أحمد: القيام قبل الصيام
proofs.note: Kashshāf gives the same precaution rationale with Aḥmad's word. qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Restricting the ruling to the text: the precautionary fast is what the naṣṣ gives, and other rulings of the month are not established, so the night stays on its original status
proofs.excerpt_ar: وظاهره أنها لا تصلى التراويح ليلتئذ، واختاره التميميون اقتصارا على النص
proofs.note: The second wajh (Abū Ḥafṣ, the Tamīmīs): no tarāwīḥ, keeping to the text. I read «iqtiṣāran ʿalā al-naṣṣ» as leaving everything beyond the fast on its prior state (the month not yet established): istishab. It could also be read as a bare restriction of the ruling, i.e. qiyas.

proofs.dalil: One narrator establishes the ḥadīth, and the divorce suspended on it follows as a dependent, though divorce is not established by one man's report
proofs.excerpt_ar: فرواه واحد ثبت الحديث به ووقع الطلاق وإن كان الطلاق لا يثبت بخلاف واحد ذكره ابن عقيل
proofs.who: Ibn Rajab, Taqrīr al-Qawāʿid (reporting Ibn ʿAqīl, ʿUmad al-Adilla)
proofs.note: Ibn ʿAqīl's ruling rests on the qāʿida that a thing is established as a dependent which is not established independently. A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Takhrīj from the next case: the oath that he usurped nothing, where the usurpation proven by a witness and oath does not bring the divorce
proofs.excerpt_ar: ويتخرج عدم وقوع الطلاق في المسألتين من المسألة الآتية
proofs.note: Non-occurrence is derived by analogy with the usurpation case (aṣl), whose ʿilla is that divorce is not proven by evidence that does not prove divorce: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Divorce is not proven by evidence that proves only property (a man and two women, a witness and oath, refusal to swear)
proofs.excerpt_ar: لم تطلق) لأن الطلاق لا يثبت بذلك والأصل بقاء العصمة
proofs.note: The divorce does not follow: what proves the usurpation does not prove divorce. A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: The original state is that the marriage tie continues
proofs.excerpt_ar: لأن الطلاق لا يثبت بذلك والأصل بقاء العصمة ولو حلف لا يستحق على فلان شيئا
proofs.note: The second reason in the same sentence: «al-aṣl baqāʾ al-ʿiṣma»: istishab.

proofs.dalil: Aḥmad's naṣṣ (riwāya of Muhannā): he said 'if you menstruate, you and your co-wife are divorced', and women testified to her menstruation; both were divorced
proofs.excerpt_ar: ويشهد له نص أحمد في رواية مهنا إذا قال لها إن حضت فأنت وضرتك طالق فشهد النساء بحيضها طلقتا جميعا
proofs.note: The divorce follows the birth proven by women. Ibn Rajab supports it with Aḥmad's naṣṣ on menstruation proven by women. Carrying that naṣṣ over to the birth case is qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Takhrīj: no divorce until those testify whose testimony proves divorce itself, as when an oath that he usurped nothing meets usurpation proven by a man and two women or a witness and oath
proofs.excerpt_ar: ويتخرج أن لا تطلق حتى يشهد من يثبت ابتداء الطلاق بشهادته، كمن حلف بالطلاق ما غصب
proofs.note: al-Majd's derived wajh, by analogy with the usurpation case: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: The dispute is over paying money, and money is proven by a witness and oath; the manumission follows from the original contract, as lineage follows a birth proven by one woman
proofs.excerpt_ar: وصار حرا وهذا قول الشافعي - رضي الله عنه -؛ لأن النزاع بينهما في أداء المال، والمال يقبل فيه الشاهد واليمين
proofs.note: al-Khiraqī's ruling (al-Shāfiʿī agrees): he is freed. A stated ʿilla (the testimony is about property): qiyas.

proofs.dalil: One witness can establish what then entails a thing that needs two, as one woman's testimony to a birth entails lineage
proofs.excerpt_ar: ولا يمتنع أن يثبت بشهادة الواحد ما يترتب عليه أمر لا يثبت إلا بشاهدين، كما أن الولادة تثبت بشهادة المرأة الواحدة
proofs.note: The tabaʿ analogy with lineage through birth: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Same: the dispute is over payment of money, which this evidence proves
proofs.excerpt_ar: وعتق) لأن النزاع بينهما في أداء المال، والمال يقبل فيه ذلك، وقيل: في غير النجم الأخير
proofs.note: al-Mubdiʿ repeats the ʿilla and notes a variant («wa-qīla») excluding the last instalment. qiyas.

proofs.dalil: The purpose of this testimony is manumission, which is not proven by a witness and oath
proofs.excerpt_ar: فإن قيل: القصد بهذه الشهادة العتق، وهو مما لا يثبت بشاهد ويمين
proofs.note: al-Mughnī raises this as an objection («fa-in qīla») and answers it. It is the only reason given anywhere for the other wajh in al-Targhīb. A rationale: qiyas. al-Mughnī's answer is a rebuttal and is not recorded.

proofs.dalil: ʿUmar's will: «This is what ʿAbd Allāh ʿUmar, Commander of the Faithful, bequeathed: if anything befalls him, Thamgh is a ṣadaqa…» (Abū Dāwūd), cited by Aḥmad; it became widely known among the Companions and no one objected
proofs.excerpt_ar: وهذا نص في مسألتنا، ووقفه هذا كان بأمر النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ولأنه اشتهر في الصحابة، فلم ينكر، فكان إجماعا
proofs.note: A waqf suspended on death, done by ʿUmar. al-Mughnī calls it a naṣṣ on the masʾala and a tacit consensus («lam yunkar»). A tacit consensus of the ṣaḥāba with none disagreeing: fatwaSahabi, not ijma.

proofs.dalil: It is a gift suspended on death, so it is valid, like an outright gift or ṣadaqa; a bequest is wider than dealings in life
proofs.excerpt_ar: ولأن هذا تبرع معلق بالموت، فصح كالهبة والصدقة المطلقة، أو نقول: صدقة معلقة بالموت، فأشبهت غير الوقف
proofs.note: Analogy with gifts and ṣadaqa, and with bequests: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: It is a bequest, and bequests accept suspension
proofs.excerpt_ar: والأول أصح ; لأنها وصية والوصايا تقبل التعليق
proofs.note: Ibn Rajab's tarjīḥ of al-manṣūṣ: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: It suspends a waqf on a condition, and suspending a waqf is not allowed, as when it is suspended on a condition during life
proofs.excerpt_ar: وقال القاضي: لا يصح هذا؛ لأنه تعليق للوقف على شرط، وتعليق الوقف على شرط غير جائز
proofs.note: al-Qāḍī's argument, with the waqf suspended on a condition during life as the aṣl: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: The divorce includes a choice (ikhtiyār) of the wife, and choice cannot be suspended on a condition
proofs.excerpt_ar: والثاني، لا يصح؛ لأن الطلاق يتضمن الاختيار، والاختيار لا يصح تعليقه بالشرط
proofs.note: The wajh that it is not valid. A stated rationale (the choice is like a contract and does not accept taʿlīq): qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Same: divorce here is choice, and choice is not attached to a condition
proofs.excerpt_ar: أحدهما: لا يصح ; لأن الطلاق اختيار والاختيار لا يتعلق بالشرط
proofs.note: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Divorce may be suspended on a condition, and it includes choosing her, so each wife who converts is chosen and divorced
proofs.excerpt_ar: أحدهما، يصح؛ لأن الطلاق يصح تعليقه بالشرط، ويتضمن الاختيار لها، فكلما أسلمت واحدة كان اختيارا لها
proofs.note: The wajh that it is valid: choice comes in as part of the divorce. A rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Divorce accepts suspension, and the choice is established as its dependent and within it
proofs.excerpt_ar: والثاني: يصح ; لأن الطلاق يقبل التعليق والاختيار يثبت تبعا له وضمنا
proofs.note: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: The lot has a role in telling free from slave, but none in determining lineage
proofs.excerpt_ar: وقيل: لا يثبتان ; لأنه لا مدخل للقرعة في تمييز النسب، ولها مدخل في تمييز الرق من الحرية
proofs.note: The view that neither lineage nor inheritance follows (al-Sāmarrī). A stated rationale: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Same: the lot has no role in lineages
proofs.excerpt_ar: أنه لا يثبت نسبه ولا يرث به وهو الذي ذكره القاضي في المجرد وابن عقيل والسامري ; لأن القرعة لا مدخل لها في الأنساب
proofs.note: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: He is free, and his freedom rests on his father's acknowledgement, so he inherits as if the father had named him in the acknowledgement
proofs.excerpt_ar: قياس المذهب ; لأنه حر استندت حريته إلى الإقرار فأشبه ما لو عينه في إقراره
proofs.note: Analogy with the child named in the acknowledgement: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Same ʿilla, given in al-Mughnī for the parallel case of one slave woman's three children and applied here: «qiyās al-madhhab» is that his lineage and inheritance are established
proofs.excerpt_ar: لأن للقرعة مدخلا في إثبات الحرية. وقياس المذهب ثبوت نسبه وميراثه، على ما ذكرنا في التي قبلها
proofs.note: al-Mughnī refers back to its argument in the preceding faṣl («he is free, his freedom resting on his father's acknowledgement, so he inherits»): qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Once the divorce is established by the lot, its consequences, the ʿidda among them, follow it
proofs.excerpt_ar: في ظاهر كلام أحمد رضي الله عنه ; لأن الطلاق لما ثبت بالقرعة تبعه لوازمه من العدة وغيرها
proofs.note: The rationale for ẓāhir kalām Aḥmad: a dependent follows what the lot establishes. qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Each wife may be the one still married, owing the death ʿidda, or the divorced one, owing the divorce ʿidda; she is free of it with certainty only by the longer of the two
proofs.excerpt_ar: لأن كل واحدة منهن يحتمل أن يكون عليها عدة الوفاة ويحتمل أنها المطلقة فعليها عدة الطلاق فلا تبرأ يقينا إلا بأطولهما
proofs.note: al-Mughnī's «wa-l-ṣaḥīḥ» for the husband dying before the divorced wife is identified: precaution for certainty. qiyas.

proofs.dalil: Same: each may be the divorced wife or another, so the longer term binds her and the shorter is included in it
proofs.excerpt_ar: تكون المطلقة أو غيرها فلزمها الأطول ودخل فيه ما دونه
proofs.note: qiyas.

proofs.dalil: In inheritance and blood money his word is accepted when it lessens his share and refused when it increases it, because he is suspect and his word does not bind others
proofs.excerpt_ar: وأما الميراث والدية، فإن أقر على نفسه بما يقلل ميراثه أو ديته، قبل منه، وإن ادعى ما يزيد ذلك، لم يقبل؛ لأنه متهم فيه
proofs.note: After accepting the hermaphrodite's word for marriage, al-Mughnī accepts it only where it is against himself. A stated ʿilla (suspicion): qiyas. No source gives a reason for all male rulings following (position 0); al-Mughnī accepts his word in his worship as a matter between him and God, but that does not cover rulings that benefit him.
